sections.label: Ageing population and chronic diseases
sections.summary: By 2030, one in four Singaporeans will be 65 and above, bringing more chronic diseases and multiple co-morbidities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: By 2030, one in four Singaporeans will be aged 65 and above.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: This substantial demographic shift brings with it a higher burden of chronic diseases and a higher proportion of patients with multiple co-morbidities.

sections.label: National Electronic Health Record system
sections.summary: Singapore has shared health information across providers since 2011 through the National Electronic Health Record system, with public hospitals contributing most beds and stays.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Singapore started sharing health information across providers since 2011, with the implementation of the National Electronic Health Record system (NEHR).

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Public hospitals contribute about 80% of total beds in Singapore and account for approximately 90% of hospital stays.

sections.label: HIB requires NEHR contribution
sections.summary: The HIB will close the remaining gap by requiring all licensed healthcare providers to contribute to and access the NEHR.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: First, the HIB will close the remaining gap by requiring all licensed healthcare providers to contribute to the NEHR and providing for their NEHR access.

sections.label: Sharing non-NEHR health information
sections.summary: The HIB will enable sharing of non-NEHR health information to facilitate community-based care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Second, the HIB will enable the sharing of non-NEHR health information to facilitate community-based care.

sections.label: Providers required to contribute health information
sections.summary: The HIB requires licensed healthcare providers and retail pharmacies to contribute key health information such as allergies, vaccinations, diagnoses, medications and test results to NEHR.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: The HIB will require all healthcare providers licensed under the Healthcare Services Act 2020 and retail pharmacies licensed under the Health Products Act 2007 to contribute key health information about patients into NEHR.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: The key health information are those crucial for continuity of care such as allergies, vaccinations, diagnoses, medications, laboratory test results, radiological images and discharge summaries.

sections.label: NEHR access for employment insurance prohibited
sections.summary: Accessing the NEHR for purposes relating to employment or insurance will be strictly prohibited.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Accessing NEHR for purposes relating to employment or insurance will be strictly prohibited.

sections.label: NEHR access for statutory examinations
sections.summary: NEHR access will be allowed for these statutory medical examinations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: NEHR access will therefore be allowed for these statutory medical examinations.

sections.label: Doctors only break glass
sections.summary: Only doctors will be allowed to break glass.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: First, only doctors will be allowed to "break glass".

sections.label: Inappropriate break-glass investigated
sections.summary: Confirmed inappropriate break-glass cases will be investigated as potential HIB breaches and may be referred to the Singapore Medical Council.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Confirmed cases of inappropriate "break-glass" will be investigated as potential breaches under the HIB and may also be referred to the Singapore Medical Council for disciplinary action.

sections.label: HIB NEHR sharing purposes
sections.summary: The HIB will provide for sharing identifiable NEHR information for public health and anonymised NEHR information for broader public interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: The HIB will provide for the sharing of identifiable NEHR information for public health purposes and anonymised NEHR information for broader public interest purposes.

sections.label: Scoped sharing without consent
sections.summary: The HIB will provide an additional data sharing channel, enabling scoped sharing of non-NEHR health information without consent if three key criteria are met.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: As mentioned earlier, the HIB will provide an additional channel for data sharing to support the goal of "One Patient, One Health Summary, One Care Journey".

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: We will enable the scoped sharing of non-NEHR health information without an individual's consent only if three key criteria are met.

sections.label: Limited shared data types
sections.summary: Shared data will generally be limited to basic identification and contact information and, if necessary, broad health risk indicators, not actual medical conditions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: The data shared will generally be limited to basic identification and contact information and if necessary, broad health risk indicators, such as the presence of frailty or chronic conditions, but not the actual medical conditions.

sections.label: Minister directions during health outages
sections.summary: Clauses 83 to 85 let the Minister direct healthcare providers to take mitigating or recovery measures during major health system outages in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Should an outage involving health information or the systems that host or process such information occur in Singapore and threaten a major disruption of healthcare services, clauses 83 to 85 will allow the Minister to direct relevant healthcare providers to take mitigating or recovery measures.

sections.label: Penalties for non-compliance with directions
sections.summary: Directions may be issued for deliberate or reckless non-compliance, and failing to comply can lead to a $20,000 fine, one year's imprisonment, or both.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: However, in the event of deliberate or reckless non-compliance or breaches, directions may then be issued to the healthcare provider to comply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: It is only when the healthcare provider fails to comply with a direction that the provider could be liable for an offence punishable by up to $20,000, one year’s imprisonment or both, upon conviction.

sections.label: Penalties for unauthorised NEHR access
sections.summary: A first offence of unauthorised NEHR access under clause 38 carries up to $50,000 fine, two years' imprisonment, or both, doubled for repeat or employment or insurance purposes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: For instance, a person convicted of an offence relating to unauthorised access of NEHR information under clause 38 faces a fine of up to $50,000, two years’ imprisonment or both, for a first offence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: This maximum penalty is doubled for a repeat offence or if the unauthorised access was for employment or insurance purposes.

sections.label: Fines for missing HIB security measures
sections.summary: Healthcare providers failing to put in place required cybersecurity or data security measures under the HIB may face a fine of up to $1 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: For instance, healthcare providers that fail to put in place the cybersecurity or data security measures required under the HIB may face a fine of up to $1 million, as the health information of many patients could be compromised.

sections.label: Bill's statutory framework for health information
sections.summary: The Bill establishes a statutory framework governing how selected health information is collected, accessed, used and shared for treatment, community health, preventive care and population well-being.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: As MOH puts it: “One Patient, One Health Summary, One Care Journey”.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This Bill establishes a statutory framework governing how selected health information is collected, accessed, used and shared – not just for medical treatment but also for community health, preventive care and population well-being.

sections.label: HIB sharing and Woodlands project
sections.summary: The HIB lets essential health information follow patients, enables sharing outside the NEHR for Healthier SG and Age Well SG, and supports the Woodlands project.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The HIB strengthens this foundation by ensuring that essential health information – medications, allergies, diagnoses – can follow the patient, not remain trapped in institutions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It enables care teams across settings to work from a shared understanding and make better clinical decisions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It also enables the sharing of health information outside the NEHR to support critical programmes, such as Healthier SG and Age Well SG.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In Woodlands, the Health Promotion Board and the National Healthcare Group have embarked on the Improving Health in Woodlands Town Project, and it has my full support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It integrates health, social and community services using shared data dashboards to guide proactive care, from identifying at-risk residents or residents with chronic diseases and connecting them to health and social services to smoothening transitions from hospital to community and home care, to promoting healthy living and to partnering with grassroots organisations and communities to curate health-related activities and link up residents to relevant interventions, supported by Community Health Dashboards for local planning and progress monitoring.

sections.label: Sensitive information authorisation
sections.summary: Sensitive information such as mental health records should require higher-level authorisation or additional justification.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Sensitive information, for instance, mental health records should require higher-level authorisation or additional justification.

sections.label: NEHR employment insurance prohibition
sections.summary: The Bill prohibits using NEHR data for employment and insurance eligibility, and indirect access or inference must be tightly controlled.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Bill rightly prohibits the use of NEHR data for employment and insurance eligibility.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Indirect access or inference – for example, where doctors are asked for medical reports or insurers rely on clinical documentation – must be tightly controlled.

sections.label: Support for smaller clinics
sections.summary: Smaller clinics and community partners must be supported, and the rate of people activating access restrictions should be tracked as a barometer of public trust.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Smaller clinics and community partners must be properly supported, not overwhelmed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: And the rate of people opting to activate access restrictions should be tracked, as a barometer of public trust.

sections.label: SingHealth patient data stolen
sections.summary: The personal particulars of 1.5 million SingHealth patients and outpatient dispensed medicine records of 160,000 patients were stolen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The personal particulars of 1.5 million SingHealth patients, including the then Prime Minister Mr Lee Hsien Loong and the records of outpatient dispensed medicines belonging to 160,000 patients were stolen.

sections.label: Neurosurgeon dismissed for record access
sections.summary: A SingHealth neurosurgeon was dismissed in 2022 for inappropriately assessing medical records of over 70 patients not under his care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: For instance, a neurosurgeon at SingHealth was dismissed in 2022 for inappropriately assessing the medical records of over 70 patients not under his care.

sections.label: Penalties under Part 2 Division 2
sections.summary: Under Part 2, Division 2, failing to comply leads to a fine not exceeding $20,000, imprisonment not exceeding 12 months, or both.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Under Part 2, Division 2, failing to comply will lead to a fine not exceeding $20,000, or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding 12 months, or to both.

sections.label: GP IT Enablement Grant limits
sections.summary: The GP IT Enablement Grant gives one-time subsidies for NEHR compatible systems but does not cover ongoing cyber security compliance costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Although the GP IT Enablement Grant offers one-time subsidies for adopting NEHR compatible system, as I understand, they do not cover the ongoing cost of maintaining cyber security compliance.

sections.label: Grant for small clinics
sections.summary: The Minister is asked to consider a grant for clinics with fewer than three full-time practitioners for ongoing HIB compliance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Given the challenges I have highlighted above, will the Minister consider giving a grant for small clinics or practices with say, fewer than three full-time practitioners to assist the clinic or doctors in their ongoing compliance, with the HIB's cyber and data standards and practices?

sections.label: SingHealth fines and HIB Section 66
sections.summary: PDPC fined SingHealth $250,000 and IHiS $750,000, totalling $1 million, and HIB Section 66 sets a $1 million maximum fine.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The Personal Data Protection Commission fined SingHealth $250,000 and its IT vendor, Integrated Health Information System (IHiS), $750,000, totalling $1 million for failing to protect 1.5 million patients' data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Section 66 of the HIB states a fine not exceeding $1 million for organisations that fail in data security in handling of health and relevant information.

sections.label: EU and California penalties
sections.summary: The EU GDPR imposes fines up to 20 million euros or 4% of worldwide turnover, and California allows class actions with US$100 to US$750 per consumer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: First, the European Union's (EU's) General Data Protection regulation imposes administrative fines of up to $20 million euros, or 4% of total worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: For a tech giant or a global hospital chain, this could amount to hundreds of millions or billions of dollars.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: This scales the penalty to the size of the entity, ensuring that the fine is never just a cost of doing business.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Another is the California Consumer Privacy Act, which allows for a private right of class action lawsuits with statutory damages between US$100 and US$750 per consumer per incident.

sections.label: SingHealth payout estimate
sections.summary: Applying that approach to the SingHealth case of 1.5 million victims would mean a payout of between $200 million and $1.5 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: If this is applied to the SingHealth case of 1.5 million victims, we will be looking at a payout of between $200 million and $1.5 billion.

sections.label: Per person fine example
sections.summary: A per person fine is illustrated by pegging it to ACRA BizFile charges of $33 or $50 per report or certificate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: By way of example, if you were to introduce say, a per person fine, similar to the approach in California – and of course, we must discuss this robustly before any decision is reached, how much this fine should be and the premises for arriving at the quantum – say, for illustrative purposes, we peg the fine per person's records to what we have to pay to acquire people's personal information from, say, the Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority's BizFile, where per report or certificate is charged at $33 or $50.

sections.label: Worker trust safeguard
sections.summary: A labour Member focuses on worker trust and the safeguard disallowing health data access or use for employment purposes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: As a labour Member, I rise today to focus on a pillar of this Bill that is essential to public confidence: worker trust, and in particular, the safeguard that disallows health data from being accessed or used for employment purposes.

sections.label: NEHR access prohibitions
sections.summary: The Bill's safeguards include specific prohibitions on NEHR access for insurance and employment purposes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The safeguards in this Bill include specific prohibitions on NEHR access for insurance and employment purposes.

sections.label: Statutory Medical Examination exceptions
sections.summary: The Bill identifies specific Statutory Medical Examinations where NEHR access is permitted, and the Member seeks assurance the list stays tightly scoped.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Not necessarily through access to records, but through fitness-for-work assessments, third-party requirements or other channels that could influence employment outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I note that the Bill identifies specific Statutory Medical Examinations where NEHR access is permitted, such as pre-enlistment checkups or assessments for vocational driving licenses.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: These are strictly defined to prevent harm to the individual or to public interest.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I seek the Minister's assurance that this list of exceptions will remain tightly scoped and will not be expanded to general pre-employment screenings without rigorous oversight.

sections.label: Health data and livelihoods
sections.summary: Safeguards prohibiting use of health data for employment purposes are important for workers, the self-employed and platform workers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Health data is intended to safeguard health, not to jeopardise livelihoods.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Therefore, safeguards that prohibit the use of health data for employment purposes are extremely important, for workers, the self-employed, and platform workers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: No worker should fear that seeking medical care could be held against them at work.

sections.label: Trust framework safeguard
sections.summary: The safeguard disallowing use of health data for employment purposes is a critical part of the trust framework.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The safeguard disallowing the use of health data for employment purposes is a critical part of our trust framework.

sections.label: Clause 30(7) data uploads
sections.summary: Clause 30(7) shows patient information continues to be uploaded to the NEHR in the background even if a restriction is in place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Notably, clause 30(7) reveals that even if a restriction is in place, a patient's information continues to be uploaded to the NEHR in the background.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This, according to MOH, is in the interest of ensuring the expeditious provision of care should the patient wish to opt-in to the NEHR in the future or during an emergency situation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But Mr Deputy Speaker, if a citizen says "no" to the NEHR today, should the state then be allowed to say, "Okay, but trust me" and collect their data anyway?

sections.label: Consent not required for data sharing
sections.summary: Patient consent is not required for sharing data between healthcare providers and public agencies under clause 50.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Notably, patient consent is also not required for the sharing of such data between healthcare providers and public agencies as established under clause 50.

sections.label: NEHR data types and access restriction
sections.summary: Clause 30(5)(a) states an access restriction does not preclude disclosure of NEHR records as derived information if the Minister approves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Type 1, which is information that is individually identifiable, as well as Type 2, data that is aggregated and anonymised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And it is worth noting that clause 30(5) paragraph (a) states that "The imposition of an access restriction does not preclude one's NEHR records, be it individually identifiable or anonymised from being disclosed as derived information, if an approval is granted by the Minister.

sections.label: Taiwan and EU health data rules
sections.summary: Taiwan and the EU have enacted regulations empowering patients to restrict use of identifiable health data for secondary purposes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For instance, both Taiwan and the EU have enacted regulations empowering patients to restrict the use of their identifiable health data for secondary purposes.

sections.label: UK Google DeepMind patient data deal
sections.summary: In 2015 the Royal Free and HS Foundation Trust signed an agreement with Google DeepMind to analyse sensitive data of 1.6 million patients.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Back in 2015, in the United Kingdom, the Royal Free and HS Foundation Trust in London signed an agreement with Google DeepMind.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This allowed the British AI firm to analyse sensitive information on 1.6 million patients who uses the TRUST hospitals each year.

sections.label: SMA survey on NEHR awareness
sections.summary: A 2018 Singapore Medical Association survey found only 50% heard of the NEHR and 14.9% fully understood it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A 2018 Singapore Medical Association survey revealed that only 50% of respondents heard about the NEHR and 14.9% fully understood what the NEHR was back then.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Will the MOH be conducting and updated public awareness survey upon implementation of the Bill to measure how public understanding of the NEHR has evolved, particularly regarding access restrictions and the use of individually identifiable data?

sections.label: Bill access restrictions clauses
sections.summary: The Bill introduces Access Restrictions under clause 29, exceptions in clause 30, and management process in clause 31.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Bill introduces Access Restrictions under clause 29, with exceptions in clause 30, and the process for managing them in clause 31.

sections.label: Class 2 Access Restrictions
sections.summary: Clause 29 allows Class 2 Access Restrictions to be prescribed by information type, user class, purpose and time period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Clause 29 allows Class 2 Access Restrictions to be prescribed by information type, user class, purpose and time period.

sections.label: Impact on solo GPs
sections.summary: It asks whether MOH assessed the full financial and operational impact on solo GPs from onboarding to ongoing cybersecurity obligations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Has MOH assessed the full financial and operational impact on solo GPs, from onboarding to ongoing cybersecurity obligations?

sections.label: Measurable usability improvements commitment
sections.summary: It asks whether MOH will commit to measurable usability improvements so that less clutter becomes a performance obligation rather than an aspiration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Will MOH commit to measurable usability improvements, such as time-to-find critical information, structured clinical summaries and clinician user experience testing so that "less clutter" becomes a performance obligation rather than an aspiration?

sections.label: Vendors fearmongering and profiteering
sections.summary: It asks how MOH will prevent digital medical records vendors from fearmongering and profiteering, pushing small clinics into expensive contracts out of fear of non-compliance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: How will MOH prevent digital medical records vendors from engaging in fearmongering and profiteering, pushing small clinics into expensive contracts out of fear of non-compliance?

sections.label: Defining reasonable safeguards
sections.summary: It asks how reasonable safeguards under clause 68 will be defined in a tiered, risk-based way.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: How will reasonable safeguards under clause 68 be defined in a tiered, risk-based way?

sections.label: Breach notification and vendor accountability
sections.summary: It asks when residents will be notified of a breach, what information and support they will receive, and how accountability will follow control where vendors or intermediaries cause cybersecurity failures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: If a breach occurs, when will residents be notified, what information will they receive and what practical support will be provided to help them protect themselves and restore trust?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Where cybersecurity failures arise from vendors or intermediaries, how will accountability follow control so that small clinics are not unfairly blamed or penalised for failures beyond their technical reach?

sections.label: Statutory framework for medical data
sections.summary: The Bill creates a statutory framework consolidating key medical data into an integrated, longitudinal view of an individual's health record.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Bill establishes a statutory framework to consolidate key medical data into an integrated, longitudinal view of an individual's health record.

sections.label: Private providers mandated to contribute
sections.summary: The Bill mandates private healthcare providers to contribute to the NEHR, which doctors can use to view medical summary information.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Following that, if you were to visit the Changi General Hospital (CGH), perhaps to see a specialist for a different medical issue, the CGH doctor will be able to use the NEHR to view the medical summary information of your SGH visit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, with this Bill, private healthcare providers will now also be mandated to contribute to the NEHR.

sections.label: Police access to NEHR data
sections.summary: A question asks whether the Police and other law enforcement agencies will be barred from using NEHR information.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I am sure that all patients appreciate the assurance that their healthcare information cannot be used for employment and insurance purposes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, I want to ask the Minister whether the Police and other law enforcement agencies will be similarly barred from using information from the NEHR?

sections.label: Recording, blocking and opting out
sections.summary: Healthcare information from every medical visit and treatment will be recorded in the NEHR, but patients can block access and opt out.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In other words, healthcare information about every medical visit and treatment in Singapore will be recorded in the NEHR, but patients can block other healthcare providers from having access to that information.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Patients wishing to opt out will also be – and here I quote directly from the Synapse FAQ – they will be "counselled, to ensure that they fully understand the implications of this decision to their care as their providers will not have access to their records." Even then, opting out does not mean your healthcare information gets deleted from the NEHR.

sections.label: Definition of notifiable data breach
sections.summary: Clause 77 identifies a notifiable data breach as one causing or likely to cause significant harm or of significant scale.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Clause 77 identifies what is a "notifiable data breach", namely, a breach which "(a) results in, or is likely to result in, significant harm to an affected individual; or (b) is, or is likely to be, of a significant scale".

sections.label: Pooled health data for researchers
sections.summary: Once fully running, citizens' pooled health data in the national electronic healthcare system will be valuable for clinical researchers and pharmaceutical companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Looking ahead, the national electronic healthcare system, once it is fully up and running, our citizen's pooled health data will be a valuable goldmine for clinical researchers and pharmaceutical companies.

sections.label: Social Dividend for commercial research
sections.summary: The Government should consider a Social Dividend so benefits of commercial research data return to the people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Moreover, if the data is used for commercial research, the Government should consider a "Social Dividend" which ensures that the benefits return to the people.

sections.label: NEHR Bill framework and excluded purposes
sections.summary: The Bill governs the NEHR framework to enable clinical care, improve coordination and consolidate care across healthcare settings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: I make this declaration, as I will be addressing certain points relating to the "excluded purposes" contained in clause 6 of the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: This Bill will govern the framework of our NEHR to: one, enable more effective clinical care; two, improve coordination; and three, consolidate care across different healthcare settings.

sections.label: No patient agreement required
sections.summary: The Bill does not require patient agreement to upload key health information onto the NEHR.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Set against this background, the Bill however, does not require patient agreement to upload the key health information onto the NEHR.

sections.label: Blanket exclusions for employment and insurance
sections.summary: Excluded purposes cover employment and insurance, and are blanket exclusions even if an individual consents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: As things stand, these are when accessing the NEHR for: one, employment; or two, insurance purposes which include when an employer decides to employ, promote or terminate an employee and when an insurer decides whether to insure, continue or renew a policy and during the processing of claims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: The excluded clauses are, in fact, what I would describe as blanket exclusions, in that, even if an individual consents or agrees to allow access for these excluded purposes, healthcare providers are not permitted to do so.

sections.label: No option to consent
sections.summary: The Bill provides no option for individuals to consent, and healthcare providers cannot access NEHR for excluded purposes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: For example, this could be for medical histories of heart conditions or cancers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: However, as the Bill currently stands, there is no such option.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Even if an individual wishes to consent, the healthcare provider is not permitted to access NEHR for the excluded purposes.

sections.label: Court-ordered access in disputes
sections.summary: In a legal dispute between insurer and insured, the Court can order access to NEHR records during discovery.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: If a legal dispute arises in the Courts between an insurer and insured, say, on issues relating to the non-declaration of relevant medical history, the Court can order access to a party’s NEHR records as part of the discovery of evidence process.

sections.label: Reviewing approach after implementation
sections.summary: Suggests starting with the current approach and reviewing it as the ecosystem takes shape after implementation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Perhaps we could start with the current approach and review this as the ecosystem takes shape after implementation.

sections.label: Three sets of concerns
sections.summary: The speaker lists three concerns: cybersecurity burden on small providers, uploading sensitive medical information despite objections, and insurance loopholes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: From my conversations with practitioners and from my reading of the Bill, I have three sets of concerns: (a) the disproportionate cybersecurity burden on small providers; (b) the uploading of sensitive medical information despite patient objections; and (c) possible insurance loopholes that may render our privacy protections ineffective.

sections.label: Bill obligations and penalties
sections.summary: The Bill designates all Healthcare Services Act licensees as relevant persons with statutory obligations and severe penalties for non-compliance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Bill designates all Healthcare Services Act licensees – from tertiary hospitals employing thousands to single-doctor GP clinics in HDB heartlands – as "relevant persons" under section 64.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: All face the same statutory obligations: to implement reasonable controls for secure processing, reasonable safeguards against unauthorised access and cybersecurity protections under sections 66 and 68.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The penalties for non-compliance are severe; fines up to $200,000 or two years' imprisonment for individuals, and up to $1 million for other entities.

sections.label: Challenges for small practitioners
sections.summary: Most primary care clinics contribute to the NEHR, but this figure masks significant challenges faced by small practitioners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: While most primary care clinics are already contributing to the NEHR, this figure masks significant challenges faced by small practitioners.

sections.label: Funding guidelines before 2027
sections.summary: Asks whether MOH would publish funding guidelines, eligibility criteria and application timeline before the Bill takes effect from early 2027.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Would MOH publish clear funding guidelines, eligibility criteria and the application timeline before the Bill takes effect from early 2027?

sections.label: Shared service models for clinics
sections.summary: Suggests MOH could facilitate or fund shared service models where three to five GP clinics jointly employ a rotating trained data coordinator.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: For example, MOH could facilitate or fund shared service models where three to five GP clinics in the same geographical cluster jointly employ a trained data coordinator who rotates between clinics, ensuring accurate and timely NEHR contribution, conducting staff training and maintaining compliance with cybersecurity protocols.

sections.label: Bill limits data sharing
sections.summary: The Bill currently limits data sharing to public sector entities, healthcare clusters and public agencies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The Bill currently limits data sharing to public sector entities – AIC, healthcare clusters and public agencies.

sections.label: Guidelines on health records
sections.summary: The Ministry appointed a Workgroup that issued guidelines on professional responsibilities for contributing to, accessing and using national health records.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Through various stakeholder consultations, the Ministry came to realise that many medical practitioners had concerns about the potential increase in medico-legal liabilities arising from the mandatory contribution of health information and the wider accessibility of that information to other healthcare providers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And so, in late 2022/early 2023, the Ministry appointed the National Electronic Health Record Guidelines Workgroup and tasked the Workgroup to come up with a set of guidelines that would provide clarity on the professional responsibilities and obligations of healthcare professionals in terms of their contribution to, access and use of our national health records.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Workgroup, which I co-chaired, has since completed its work and issued a set of guidelines setting out the core ethical principles relating to our national health records, and proposing reasonable professional standards to be observed by all contributors and users.

sections.label: Patient interests and access restrictions
sections.summary: The Bill addresses patient autonomy and sensitivities, providing access restrictions and barring access for employment or insurance purposes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We also took into account the interests of patients, the need to respect their autonomy in terms of who they would grant access to their national health records and the sensitivities associated with certain types of health information, for example, conditions that are stigmatising or affect employment opportunities or one's insurability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am heartened to see that these issues have been specifically addressed in the Bill, which provides for access restrictions and makes it clear that access to our national health records should not be for employment or insurance purposes.

sections.label: Flexibility for teething problems
sections.summary: Senior Ministry officers signalled flexibility and allowances for non-compliance due to teething problems in the initial stages.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I can attest to the fact that senior Ministry officers who were present to hear these concerns from the ground have been extremely understanding and reassuring.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They have signalled that flexibility will be exercised and allowances given in the event of non-compliance due to teething problems during the initial stages, and these problems could include delays in implementing adequate systemic safeguards.

sections.label: Bill takes effect 2027
sections.summary: The Bill takes effect from 2027, giving healthcare providers time to adopt support measures and comply.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Bill takes effect from 2027, providing healthcare providers time to adopt support measures and comply with requirements.

sections.label: Reporting significant data breaches
sections.summary: Healthcare providers must report data breaches to MOH and affected individuals if the breaches result in significant harm.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Healthcare providers must report data breaches to MOH and affected individuals if the breaches result in significant harm.

sections.label: Patient breach notification and access logs
sections.summary: Patients should be notified of significant breaches and be able to view access logs and flag suspicious activity to MOH.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Two, patients should be notified of significant breaches affecting any number of individuals.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Four, patients should be able to view access logs for their records and flag suspicious activity to MOH.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: With targeted support for community practitioners, robust data transition frameworks, enhanced support for AHPs and clear safeguards for smaller data breaches, this Bill can deliver genuine benefits while protecting patient privacy and maintaining trust.

sections.label: Offence to access NEHR
sections.summary: Clause 38 makes it an offence to access the NEHR for these purposes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Haresh Singaraju (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Clause 38 makes it an offence to access the NEHR, for these purposes.

sections.label: Good faith protection undefined
sections.summary: Clause 99 protects those acting in good faith and with reasonable care but does not define reasonable care.

sentences.speaker: Dr Haresh Singaraju (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Clause 99 protects those who act in good faith and with reasonable care, but it does not define what reasonable care looks like.

sections.label: Small practices face same standards
sections.summary: Solo and small group GP practices face the same data security and breach reporting standards with fewer resources.

sentences.speaker: Dr Haresh Singaraju (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The solo GP in Bedok, the small group practice in Jurong: they face the same data security and breach reporting standards under Parts 4 and 5, with far fewer resources.

sections.label: Portability and care relationships
sections.summary: The speaker asks what measures will ensure portability reinforces rather than weakens care relationships Healthier SG seeks to build.

sentences.speaker: Dr Haresh Singaraju (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Episodic care from whichever provider is nearest, cheapest or most convenient, leading to wasted resources.

sentences.speaker: Dr Haresh Singaraju (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I ask the Minister: what measures will ensure that portability reinforces, rather than weakens, the care relationships Healthier SG seeks to build?

sections.label: NEHR legal footing and safeguards
sections.summary: The Bill lowers risks of missed allergies, drug interactions and repeated tests, and puts the NEHR on clearer legal footing.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It also lowers the risk of missed allergies, drug interactions and also unnecessary repeated tests that cost time, money and anxiety.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This Bill puts the NEHR system on a clearer legal footing, including governance of access, use and safeguards.

sections.label: NEHR clinical care reassurance
sections.summary: MOH stated NEHR information is for clinical care and is not accessible by employers or insurers.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In addition, it is important to reassure Singaporeans clearly by proactively communicating the following, that MOH has stated that NEHR's information is for clinical care and is not accessible by employers or insurers.

sections.label: EMR access not in history
sections.summary: Accesses made in providers' own EMR systems are not included in the NEHR Access History.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Accesses made to your records in their own EMR systems are not included in the National Electronic Health Record Access History." In plain English, what it means is that sometimes doctors and nurses, they see your records through their own systems rather than the NEHR.

sections.label: MOH encouraging compliance on core data
sections.summary: MOH is asked how it would encourage compliance for core data such as medication lists, vaccinations and dental notes.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In our case, beyond reporting required by law, how would MOH encourage strong compliance in the everyday operations, that is required in the core data that is reflected in our Bill, such as medication list, vaccinations administered and also dental notes, and so on.

sections.label: Cybersecurity obligations for smaller clinics
sections.summary: Cybersecurity audit and reporting obligations are necessary but operationally demanding, and smaller clinics may need more time and support.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Cybersecurity audit and reporting obligations are necessary, but they are operationally demanding.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Smaller clinics and some community providers may need more time and practical support to meet new requirements properly.

sections.label: Overseas health information capture
sections.summary: Information generated overseas will not automatically be captured in the national health record system.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: For instance, with the initiative such as the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone and the MOU on Corporation in Health signed in December 2025, I think we are likely to see closer health linkages and maybe more Singaporeans might go up north for medical screening and treatments in the near future.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: However, information generated overseas will not automatically be captured in our national health record system, so I would like to seek the Ministry's view on information generated overseas.

sections.label: NEHR as supplementary clinical tool
sections.summary: The Minister is asked to confirm the NEHR is a supplementary clinical tool, not a mandatory step in every consultation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Can the Minister confirm that the NEHR is positioned as a supplementary clinical tool, and not a mandatory step that must be accessed in every single consultation?

sections.label: Employment and insurance access prohibited
sections.summary: The Bill prohibits access for employment and insurance purposes, except in narrowly defined statutory medical examinations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Crucially, the Bill explicitly prohibits access for employment and insurance purposes, except in narrowly defined statutory medical examinations.

sections.label: Patient access controls and emergencies
sections.summary: Patients can see who accessed their records, restrict access, and flag misuse, while critical health information and emergency access remain available.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Patients will be able to see who has accessed their records, restrict access where appropriate, and flag potential misuse.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Even when patients apply restrictions, a core set of critical health information, and full access in genuine medical emergencies, will remain available.

sections.label: Safeguards for dignity and trust
sections.summary: Safeguards protect dignity and trust, ensuring clinicians have right information and patients retain privacy and autonomy, so the member supports the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Such safeguards are critical in protecting dignity and sustaining trust, especially for patients who already feel vulnerable at the point of care.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: It is about ensuring that clinicians have the right information at the right time, that patients retain dignity, privacy and autonomy, and that trust remains the foundation of our healthcare system.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: For any healthcare system to function well, healthcare providers must trust the system, patients must trust the system and the healthcare system must be worthy of that trust.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: With the safeguards for patients, clarity for providers, and support for implementation, I support this Bill.

sections.label: Penalties for unauthorised NEHR access
sections.summary: First-time unauthorised NEHR access carries a maximum fine of $50,000 and/or up to two years' imprisonment, doubled for repeat offenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: First-time offences of unauthorised access of NEHR are punishable with a maximum fine of $50,000 and/or up to two years' imprisonment upon conviction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: And the penalty is doubled for repeat offenders.

sections.label: Synapxe audits and monitoring
sections.summary: Synapxe, the NEHR system operator, conducts regular audits and ongoing monitoring to detect suspicious behaviour or atypical patterns, including from patient alerts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Synapxe, the NEHR system operator, conducts regular audits and ongoing monitoring to detect suspicious behaviour or atypical patterns, including in response to patient alerts.

sections.label: NEHR Access History in HealthHub
sections.summary: Access to a patient's NEHR information over the preceding 12 months is made known through the HealthHub application's NEHR Access History feature.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: In addition, instances when a patient's NEHR information is accessed over the preceding 12 months will be made known to him through the "NEHR Access History" feature in the HealthHub application.

sections.label: Patient access restrictions in Bill
sections.summary: The HIB allows patients to restrict healthcare providers from accessing their NEHR information, called Access Restrictions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: To assuage the concerns of these patients, the HIB will allow patients to restrict healthcare providers from accessing their NEHR information or we call this "Access Restrictions" in the Bill.

sections.label: Restricting NEHR access to providers
sections.summary: Patients may restrict all providers, or from second half of 2026 limit access to select providers, except allergy and vaccination records.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Patients may, however, restrict access to all healthcare providers, or from the second half of 2026, limit access so that only select healthcare providers, such as their own Healthier SG clinic, may access their NEHR information.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Whilst in place, restricted healthcare providers will not be able to, unless required by other written law, access the patient's NEHR information, except for the essential subset of records that cover allergies and vaccination records.

sections.label: Insurers and employers lack access
sections.summary: Insurers and employers do not and will not have access to NEHR.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: First, insurers and employers do not and will not have access to NEHR.

sections.label: Scope of statutory medical examinations
sections.summary: The Bill's list of statutory medical examinations is tightly scoped to those where NEHR access is necessary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: The list of statutory medical examinations that is in the Bill is tightly scoped to those where NEHR access is necessary to protect the public and safeguard the health of the individual.

sections.label: No access for insurance checks
sections.summary: NEHR must not be accessed for insurance- and employment-related checks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: NEHR must not be accessed for such insurance- and employment-related checks.

sections.label: Providers must contribute health information
sections.summary: The Bill requires healthcare providers to contribute accurate and complete health information in a timely manner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: The Bill requires healthcare providers to contribute accurate and complete health information in a timely manner.

sections.label: Prison inmates NEHR inclusion
sections.summary: All Singaporeans' key health information, including those under Singapore Prison Service care, will be contributed to NEHR.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: To Dr Hamid's query on whether populations who receive care outside the conventional system, such as prison inmates, would benefit from the Bill, I would like to assure the Member that all Singaporeans key health information, including those under the care of the Singapore Prison Service, will be contributed to NEHR.

sections.label: Consultation before NEHR access changes
sections.summary: Before changing which providers may access NEHR, MOH will consult stakeholders and communicate changes publicly via its website.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Prior to changing the scope of providers that may access NEHR, we will consult relevant stakeholders and publicly communicate the changes through the MOH website.

sections.label: De-identified NEHR data sharing
sections.summary: De-identified NEHR data may be shared for research via platforms like TRUST, with commercial requests assessed cautiously.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: De-identified NEHR health information may be shared through established platforms such as TRUST under the National Research Foundation for research purposes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Where requests are received from commercial parties, possibly for commercial purposes, we are extremely cautious in assessing such requests, including whether the sharing of such data is helpful in contributing to better healthcare and better health outcomes.

sections.label: NEHR security and resilience audits
sections.summary: NEHR undergoes regular security and resilience audits, vulnerability scans, penetration tests and exercises to keep systems secure and backups operational.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: NEHR is subject to security and resilience audits, with vulnerability scans, penetration tests and exercises carried out regularly to ensure that systems are secure and backup systems are operational in the event of a downtime.

sections.label: Notification of significant data breaches
sections.summary: Healthcare providers must notify MOH and affected individuals of significant data breaches.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Healthcare providers will be required to notify MOH and affected individuals of significant data breaches.

sections.label: Defining significant harm in breaches
sections.summary: If a breach causes or likely causes significant harm, providers must notify affected individuals on or after notifying MOH.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: To Mr Fadli Fawzi's query on how significant harm will be defined, if a data breach causes or is likely to cause significant harm to an individual, for example, if it involves disclosure of health information that may be deemed more sensitive, healthcare providers must notify the affected individuals on or after notifying MOH.

sections.label: Support for HIMS subscription costs
sections.summary: A support package will include measures to defray costs of subscribing to whitelisted HIB-compliant HIMS for clinical records and NEHR data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Our support package will include measures to defray costs of subscription to whitelisted HIB-compliant HIMS to digitalise their clinical records and to contribute data to NEHR more seamlessly.

sections.label: Healthier SG clinics on Clinic Management Systems
sections.summary: About 1,100 Healthier SG clinics are onboard suitable Clinic Management Systems and contribute to NEHR.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Today, about 1,100 Healthier SG clinics are onboard suitable Clinic Management Systems and contribute to NEHR.

sections.label: Bill commencement, guidance and compliance support
sections.summary: The Bill commences in early 2027, guidance and support channels start in the second quarter, and MOH will consider each compliance case.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: First, the Bill will commence in early 2027 to allow sufficient time for healthcare providers and professionals to familiarise themselves with the Bill's requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Second, to support their transition, guidance materials and dedicated support channels will be made available from the second quarter of this year to help providers and professionals understand their options and navigate the process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Third, should there be challenges complying with the Bill by the required timelines, MOH will consider the facts of each case carefully and assist where appropriate.

sections.label: Guidelines for NEHR information access
sections.summary: MOH will publish guidelines to support healthcare professionals' appropriate access and use of NEHR information.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: MOH will publish a set of guidelines to support healthcare professionals' appropriate access and use of NEHR information.

sections.label: Cybersecurity insurance and GP flexibility
sections.summary: Cybersecurity insurance will be considered, funding and whitelisting will support senior and smaller GPs, but standards will not differ by clinic size.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: In terms of cybersecurity insurance, this is something we certainly will consider, but today, unfortunately, there is not a very mature market for cybersecurity insurance, specifically for GPs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Second, about flexibility for senior GPs or smaller GPs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: We do intend to provide for them, including funding support, whitelisting service providers and the different mentioned systems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: But I think what we want to avoid is having different standards of cybersecurity and data security requirements for different clinics based on the size.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: I think that is not the sensible and practical way to do it, as mentioned by different Members earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: It is about making sure that different clinics and different touch points to the NEHR system meet the appropriate level of cybersecurity and data security requirements and finding ways of uplifting the different GPs and we will certainly do so in the coming months and years.

sections.label: Insurance regulation and NEHR prohibition
sections.summary: MOH is working with providers, industry associations and MAS on insurance regulation, while the HIB prohibits NEHR use for employment and insurance purposes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: On a dedicated regulation around insurance, whether they should just be prohibited, to avoid putting the healthcare providers or professionals in a very difficult situation – this is something we are working through with the healthcare providers, the industry associations as well as together with MAS with the insurance industry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: We will certainly work closely with MAS as the regulator for the insurance industry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: But I think, it is quite clear, the principle and approach under the HIB is that we prohibit the use and access of NEHR information for employment and insurance purposes.

sections.label: NEHR and EMR access logging
sections.summary: Access to NEHR through the EMR is logged as NEHR access, while accessing records on institutions' own EMR systems is separate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Access to NEHR, even through the EMR, will be logged as an access to NEHR.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: But accessing a patient's records on the healthcare institutions' own EMR system is separate.
